question_text: Visual Basic is described in the course guide as an event-driven language which has some features of:
explanation: Visual Basic is an event-driven language with some features of Object Oriented Programming (OOP), where actions are tied to the occurrence of events like a mouse click.

question_text: In Visual Basic, a "project" is best described as:
option_a: A single standalone file with no other components
option_b: A collection of files that make up your application
explanation: A project is a collection of files that make up an application; a single application might consist of several files, which together form the project.

question_text: The Visual Basic Toolbox is best described as:
option_b: A collection of tools that act as a repository of controls you can place on a form
explanation: The Toolbox is a window containing a collection of tools that act as a repository of controls (such as labels, buttons, and text boxes) that can be placed on a form.

question_text: Visual Basic has a total of four toolbars: Debug, Edit, Standard, and:
explanation: The four Visual Basic toolbars are Debug (for tracing and correcting problems), Edit (aids code editing), Form Editor (adjusts objects on forms), and Standard (the default toolbar).

question_text: When a control is selected on a Visual Basic form, the Properties window:
option_b: Changes to list every property related to that selected control
option_c: Only shows properties for the entire project, not individual controls
option_d: Can only be used to delete the control
explanation: When you select a control, the Properties window changes to list every property related to that specific control, allowing you to modify its values.

question_text: In the Visual Basic Project window, related components are listed in a tree-structured format that can include Forms, Modules, and:
explanation: The Project window lists components in a tree-structured listing, including Projects, Forms, Modules, Class modules, User controls, User documents, and Property pages.

question_text: To display the Menu Editor from the Form window in Visual Basic, you press:
explanation: From the Form window, you can press Ctrl+E to display the Menu Editor, which helps design menus for Visual Basic applications.

question_text: In a Visual Basic menu caption, an ampersand (&) placed before a letter indicates:
option_a: That the letter will be hidden from the user entirely
option_b: The underscored accelerator key letter, allowing the option to be selected with Alt plus that letter
option_c: A syntax error in the program
option_d: That the menu item cannot be clicked
explanation: The ampersand next to a letter indicates the accelerator key; for example, "&New" means the option appears as "New" and can be selected by pressing Alt+N.

question_text: The Visual Basic Code window contains several sections, including the declarations section, general-purpose procedures, and:
option_a: Event procedures, which execute after actions like a mouse click or form load
explanation: The Code window's sections include the declarations section, general-purpose procedures (which perform any kind of function), and event procedures (executed after events like clicking or loading a form).

question_text: When saving a Visual Basic project, the project description file is saved with the filename extension:
explanation: Selecting File, Save Project saves every file inside the project as well as a project description file with the filename extension VBP.
